title: Utility Order for Entergy Louisiana, LLC, ex parte. — This order accepts the Stipulation filed into the record on September 4, 2026 regarding AEO information, vacates the ALJ's Ruling issued on August 6, 2026, and renders ELL's Motion for Immediate Review moot.  This matter was considered at the Commission's September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                       ORDER NUMBER U-37882-B

                             ENTERGY LOUISIANA, LLC, EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-37882, In re: Application for certification of generation and transmission
resources and for other relief.

                (Decided at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                                     ORDER

    I.       BACKGROUND AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY

         On March 25, 2026, Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL”) filed its Application of Entergy

Louisiana, LLC for Certification of Generation and Transmission Resources and for other Relief

Pursuant to the Commission’s Lightning Initiative (“Application”) before the Louisiana Public

Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”).                         In its Application, ELL sought the

Commission’s approval to add 5,278 megawatts (“MW”) of generation, in addition to battery

storage and transmission, to serve Evest LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Meta Platforms, Inc.

(“Meta”). According to the Application, Evest LLC is locating a large hyperscale data center in

Richland Parish, Louisiana, adjacent to the facility approved in Commission Order No. U-37425

for Meta subsidiary, Laidley, LLC.1

         The Application was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin No. 1372 dated

March 27, 2026, for a 15-day intervention period. The Alliance for Affordable Energy and the

Union of Concerned Scientists (“collectively, “the NPOs”) intervened in the proceeding, along

with the Louisiana Energy Users Group (“LEUG”), Southern Renewable Energy Association

(“SREA”), Sierra Club, the Association of Louisiana Electric Cooperatives, Inc., 1803 Electric

Cooperative, Inc., Walmart Inc., and Gulf States Renewable Energy Industries Association.

         On July 15, 2026, the NPOs filed its Motion of the Alliance for Affordable Energy and

Union of Concerned Scientists for Access to "Attorney’s Eyes Only" Information ("AEO Motion"),

wherein the NPOs sought access to Attorney’s Eyes Only (“AEO”) information for certain

representatives (the “HSPM Designees”).




1 See Order No. U-37425 - Entergy Louisiana, LLC, ex parte. In re: Application for approval of generation and

transmission resources in connection with service to a single customer for a project in North Louisiana, issued August
29, 2025. In Order No. U-37425 the Commission accepted the settlement entered into by ELL, LPSC Staff, Sierra
Club, Walmart, and Southern Renewable Energy Association, approving the generation and transmission resources
proposed in connection with service to a customer project in North Louisiana, subject to certain conditions.

                                                                                          Order No. U-37882-B
                                                                                                       Page 1
        In the AEO Motion, the NPOs asserted, amongst other things, that they cannot fully

participate in the case when the HSPM Designees are not allowed to review large portions of the

filing, or to review the entirety of their own experts’ testimony. Further, the NPOs argued that

restricting their access interferes with their attorney-client relationship, as counsel are unable to

fully advise their clients. The NPOs argued that there is no legitimate basis for restricting access,

given that the client representatives have signed the Confidentiality Agreement and are bound by

it. Finally, the NPOs argued that the Commission has never approved the AEO designation.

       On July 17, 2026, ELL filed Entergy Louisiana, LLC’s Memorandum in Opposition to

Motion of the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists for Access to

“Attorney’s Eyes Only” Information (“ELL Opposition”) and SREA filed Southern Renewable

Energy Association’s Response to the NPOs’ Motion for Access to “Attorney’s Eyes Only”

Information (“SREA Response”).

       The ELL Opposition noted that the AEO Motion challenges long-held Commission policy

of prohibiting the disclosure of customer-specific information. ELL argued that the AEO Motion

seeks to undo reasonable, commonsense restrictions placed upon its customer’s most private and

commercially and competitively sensitive information at the risk of allowing intervenors, who may

include competitors, access to this information. Further, ELL argued that it is unnecessary to even

consider the NPOs’ request, since by signing the Confidentiality Agreement, an unambiguous,

enforceable contract, they are bound by its terms, and have waived any argument to the contrary.

Specifically, ELL asserted that the Confidentiality Agreement defines AEO information, which is

a subset of HSPM information, and limits access to “Authorized Persons,” who are also defined

therein. Because the NPOs agreed to the terms of the CA, and that same CA limits their ability to

access AEO information, ELL contended that the NPO’s AEO Motion should be denied under the

plain language of the CA.

       In the SREA Response, SREA supported the position of the NPOs in the AEO Motion, but

clarified that the NPO client representatives were not the only individuals precluded from

reviewing the information; specifically, the material designated AEO was withheld from certain

SREA representatives. In the SREA Response, it supported and adopted the position of the NPOs,

but objected to the exclusion of the aforementioned SREA representatives, who had likewise

signed the Confidentiality Agreement and Non-Disclosure Certificate.




                                                                             Order No. U-37882-B
                                                                                          Page 2
         On July 23, 2026, the NPOs filed The Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of

Concerned Scientists’ Motion for Leave to File Reply to Entergy Louisiana’s Memorandum in

Opposition to Motion of the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists for

Access to “Attorney’s Eyes Only” Information (“NPO Reply”), which was granted, allowing for

consideration of the NPO Reply.2

        After receiving briefs from certain parties and hearing oral argument on July 29, 2026,3 the

Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”) issued the Ruling on NPO’s Motion for Access to “Attorney’s

Eyes Only” Information (“AEO Ruling”) on August 6, 2026, wherein the ALJ found that ELL

failed to meet its burden to show that the HSPM Designees’ signatures on the Confidentiality

Agreement are insufficient to receive the requested information and that an additional layer of

protection is required.

        ELL timely filed its motion entitled Entergy Louisiana, LLC’s Motion for Immediate

Review of Interlocutory Ruling and Incorporated Memorandum in Support (“Motion for

Immediate Review”) on August 11, 2026.4 ELL also filed its motion entitled Entergy Louisiana,

LLC’s Motion for Stay Pending Immediate Review by Commission Pursuant to Rule 57 (“Motion

for Stay”) that same day. The Motion for Stay was granted on August 12, 2026, and remained in

place pending Commission review of the AEO Ruling.

        The NPOs timely filed The Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned

Scientists’ Opposition to Entergy Louisiana, LLC’s Motion for Immediate Review of Interlocutory

Ruling (the “Opposition to Motion for Immediate Review”) on August 21, 2026.5

        On August 26, 2026, after considering the memoranda and argument of the parties, and in

accordance with the procedures set forth in Commission Rule 57, the ALJ issued its Referral of

Interlocutory Ruling to Commissioners for Review, wherein the ALJ declined to reconsider the

interlocutory ruling and referred the AEO Ruling to the Commissioners for immediate review.


        On September 4, 2026, ELL and the NPOs (“Stipulating Parties”) filed a Joint Motion to

Vacate August 6, 2026 Ruling Pursuant to Rule 57 (“Motion to Vacate”). The Motion to Vacate

stated that the Stipulating Parties have reached an agreement which resolves the issues raised in


2 See Ruling on Motion for Leave to File Reply and Notice of Modifications to Procedural Schedule, issued on July

22, 2026.
3 Commission Staff did not file a brief and did not take a position on the AEO Motion.
4 Rule 57 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure allows any party to apply for immediate review of

an interlocutory ruling, which may be obtained upon a showing of irreparable injury, if a motion and memorandum
is filed within ten days of the interlocutory ruling.
5 Commission Rule 57(2) provides that any party opposing a motion for immediate review may file an opposition

within ten days.

                                                                                        Order No. U-37882-B
                                                                                                     Page 3
 the NPO’s AEO Motion, as well as ELL’s Motion for Immediate Review. A copy of the

Stipulation between the Stipulating Parties was attached to the Motion to Vacate. Therefore, the

Stipulating Parties requested that the Commission vacate the ALJ’s August 6, 2026 Ruling, which

would moot ELL’s Motion for Immediate Review.


   II.       COMMISSION JURISDICTION

          The jurisdiction of the Commission is set forth by constitutional and statutory provisions.

The Louisiana Constitution, Article IV, Section 21, provides:

                 The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
                 utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
                 It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
                 procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
                 other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.


   III.      COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

          This matter was considered at the Commission’s September 16, 2026 Business and

Executive Session. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and

unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to exercise its original and primary jurisdiction

pursuant to Rule 57.

          Chairman Skrmetta made the following motion: Because ELL, the Alliance for Affordable

Energy, and the Union for Concerned Scientists have filed a Stipulation into the record on

September 4, 2026, attached to the Motion to Vacate, that resolves all issues raised in the NPO’s

AEO motion, as well as ELL’s Motion for Immediate Review, I move that we: (1) Grant the

Motion and accept the Stipulation filed into the record on September 4, 2026; (2) Vacate the

August 6, 2026 Ruling from the ALJ; and (3) Deem ELL’s pending Motion for Immediate Review

moot.

          After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and

unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept Chairman Skrmetta’s motion.




                                     [This space left intentionally blank]




                                                                               Order No. U-37882-B
                                                                                            Page 4
 THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED:

  1. The Joint Motion to Vacate August 6, 2026 Ruling Pursuant to Rule 57 filed on September
     4, 2026 is granted;

  2. The Stipulation filed into the record on September 4, 2026 is accepted;

  3. The Ruling on NPO’s Motion for Access to “Attorney’s Eyes Only” Information issued by
     the ALJ on August 6, 2026 is vacated; and,

  4. Entergy Louisiana, LLC’s Motion for Immediate Review of Interlocutory Ruling and
     Incorporated Memorandum in Support filed into the record on August 11 is deemed moot.




BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
October 16, 2026
